articles.title: Socure raises growth investment at $5.2B valuation and acquires Fravity
articles.summary: Socure announced a strategic growth investment led by Summit Partners at a $5.2 billion valuation and acquired Fravity, whose agentic fraud and compliance automation technology will be integrated into Socure's RiskOS platform as RiskOS_Agents. The company says it exited Q2 with $364 million in ARR, 63% year-over-year growth, and more than 3,000 customers, while positioning proprietary data, first-party agents, and closed-loop decisioning as the foundation for automating fraud, identity, and compliance operations.

articles.title: US appeals court rules against prediction markets, setting up likely Supreme Court fight
articles.summary: The Ninth Circuit ruled that sports-related event contracts offered by Kalshi, Crypto.com, and Robinhood are not federally regulated swaps, siding with Nevada and other states that view them as gambling products subject to state law. The decision directly conflicts with an April Third Circuit ruling, creating a circuit split that makes Supreme Court review increasingly likely and could determine whether the CFTC or state gaming regulators control the future of sports prediction markets.

articles.title: Stripe and Advent abandon $50B+ pursuit of PayPal
articles.summary: Stripe and Advent International have reportedly walked away from their more than $50 billion bid for PayPal after the company's board viewed the offer as too low, sending PayPal shares down as much as 16% in premarket trading. The failed deal leaves PayPal to continue its turnaround under CEO Enrique Lores, including a major restructuring and planned workforce cuts, though a renewed approach remains possible if conditions change.

articles.title: AI created new customer problems, and fintechs are racing to solve them
articles.summary: The biggest AI opportunities in fintech are not just using AI to improve old workflows, but solving entirely new customer problems created by AI itself, such as token spend management, model routing, agent identity, agent payments, and compute procurement. The winners will be the companies that either own the orchestration layer, control a trusted point such as identity or settlement, or become the easiest product for AI agents and control planes to call.

articles.title: Moats in the age of floods
articles.summary: Increasingly capable AI models will not eliminate the application layer because the real bottleneck is turning raw intelligence into reliable outcomes across messy workflows, institutions, incentives, and human coordination. This post outlines seven ways companies can build durable moats, including orchestrating networks, accumulating workflow data, giving customers control over AI deployments, climbing to higher-value abstractions, pricing against outcomes, and becoming a trusted layer that models alone cannot replace.

articles.title: Visa expands open-source AI cyber defence system
articles.summary: Visa today announced enhancements to its cybersecurity portfolio to help organizations identify and fix vulnerabilities more effectively.

articles.title: Affirm returns to Australia through expanded Shopify partnership
articles.summary: Affirm is re-entering Australia by expanding its Shopify partnership to bring Shop Pay Installments to local merchants, offering eligible shoppers fortnightly or monthly payment plans with upfront terms and no late fees. The launch extends Affirm's international distribution through Shopify and gives Australian merchants a native BNPL option as competition in the market continues to intensify.

articles.title: RQD Clearing raises $74M to expand modern clearing infrastructure
articles.summary: RQD Clearing raised a $74 million minority growth investment led by Bain Capital Tech Opportunities, with participation from ABN AMRO Clearing Bank and Nyca Partners, to expand across North America, Asia, and the Middle East and invest further in digital assets and tokenization. The company is positioning its proprietary, real-time clearing and custody platform as an alternative to legacy post-trade infrastructure, after processing nearly $2 trillion in US equity notional value and $3.93 trillion in options notional year to date.

articles.title: Stripe acquires Clerky to offer legal infrastructure for startups
articles.summary: The deal brings incorporation, fundraising, equity, hiring, and corporate maintenance workflows into Stripe's growing startup ecosystem. Clerky complements Stripe Atlas with deeper legal tools and attorney relationships, allowing Stripe to build ties with founders before they need payment processing and retain them as they scale.

articles.title: Young Americans become more hostile to AI, fearing job losses
articles.summary: Nearly three-quarters of adults in the US under 30 expect the technology to reduce employment opportunities, up from 61% two years ago.

articles.title: Walmart to finally start accepting Apple Pay and Google Pay
articles.summary: Tap to Pay has begun rolling out at select Walmart and Sam's Club locations.
